title: A mood dial in GPT-2 small
question: Does one direction, taken from happy-minus-angry sentences, push GPT-2's next word from 'terrible' towards 'great', how much per unit of push, and what does it break?

models.load_note: 10.5 GB free on the GPU; bf16 weights need about 1.0 GB; float32 fits, so it runs in float32

summary.headline: dose +1 shifts the metric by +7.86; random directions of the same size, at most 2.74

claims.text: Pushing along the direction at layer 6 (dose +1) shifts the metric by +7.86 (95% CI +7.01 to +8.7, over 8 prompts); 32 random directions of the same size shift it by at most 2.74. Loss on neutral text changes by +2.46 nats.
claims.test: effect CI (Student t over prompts) excludes zero, and the effect exceeds 3 sd and the maximum of the random-direction controls

claims.text: Pushing against the direction at layer 6 (dose -1) shifts the metric by -4.38 (95% CI -5.36 to -3.39, over 8 prompts); 32 random directions of the same size shift it by at most 3.43. Loss on neutral text changes by +2.64 nats.
claims.test: effect CI (Student t over prompts) excludes zero, and the effect exceeds 3 sd and the maximum of the random-direction controls

direction.note: train_auc is measured on the same examples that built the direction

metric.describe: log-prob of ' great' minus ' terrible' as the next token
